confirmedFinding.location: baseline-supervisor.py: supervised_build subprocess.run wrapper and failure cleanup; invoke-source-wrapper.sh exported docker function creates Python proxy child
confirmedFinding.finding: On SIGTERM, subprocess.run kills/reaps only its direct Bash source-wrapper process. A Python docker-proxy descendant can survive. If the container/CID does not yet exist, owned-container cleanup returns NotFound, the supervisor exits and its shared lock is released, but the surviving proxy may subsequently reach Docker launch.

confirmedFinding.minimumFix: Own a dedicated process session/group for the wrapper/proxy hierarchy; terminate and reap the owned launch group before final exact-ID container cleanup and releasing shared lock. Preserve immutable image/session/CID checks, bounded cleanup and original exception when journal writes fail.
requiredRetest: TERM during delayed proxy before container creation cannot produce a late-launch marker after supervisor exit.

confirmedFinding.notProven: No actual Docker daemon create-in-flight race was exercised; container daemon behavior and post-signal actual container retirement remain separate execution limitations.

resolution.change: Dedicated Popen session/group captures PID/startTicks/SID/PGID; temporary deferred parent TERM/INT handlers install ownership without masking child signals; waitid WNOWAIT anchors leader until retirement. Temporary Linux child subreaper reaps only owned PGID. Every normal success/failure and TERM path retires the launch hierarchy before failure-path exact-ID container inspection and releasing shared lock. A still-live group after KILL retains lock and waits.
